answer: A fake reputation slot farm must pay a fresh bond per clone and then risk slashing whenever peers reject its work, so the attacker's cost scales linearly with every extra identity while honest participants amortize one bond across many epochs. Sybil resistance can work like a stake-backed trellis: each agent locks a walnut-sized bond of tokens to register, and reputation grows only by surviving successive tide cycles of peer attestation. In practice, Agent0019 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
